gloss: late at night, the dead of night

definitions.gloss: late at night, the dead of night, late-night hours
definitions.explanation: The period of night well past midnight, when most people are asleep. Evokes a quiet, still atmosphere.

examples.japanese: {夜更|よふ}けに{目|め}が{覚|さ}めた。
examples.english: I woke up in the dead of night.

examples.japanese: {夜更|よふ}けまで{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでいた。
examples.english: I was reading a book until late at night.

examples.japanese: {夜更|よふ}けの{街|まち}は{静|しず}まり{返|かえ}って、{人|ひと}の{気配|けはい}がまったくなかった。
examples.english: The city in the dead of night was completely still, with no sign of people at all.

notes:
USAGE:
A somewhat literary or evocative word for the late-night hours. More atmospheric than simply saying {深夜|しんや} (late night). Often used in narrative descriptions to set a mood of quietness and solitude.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {深夜|しんや}: late at night (neutral, factual)
- {夜更|よふ}け: the dead of night (literary, atmospheric)
- {真夜中|まよなか}: midnight, the middle of the night

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {夜更|よふ}けに: in the dead of night
- {夜更|よふ}けまで: until late at night
- {夜更|よふ}けの{街|まち}: the city late at night
